definition: In machine learning and computational learning theory, LogitBoost is a boosting algorithm formulated by Jerome Friedman, Trevor Hastie, and Robert Tibshirani.
details: The original paper casts the AdaBoost algorithm into a statistical framework. Specifically, if one considers AdaBoost as a generalized additive model and then applies the cost function of logistic regression, one can derive the LogitBoost algorithm.

explainer.lead: LogitBoost is a boosting algorithm from Friedman, Hastie and Tibshirani that casts AdaBoost in a statistical framework. It matters because it connects boosting to logistic regression, giving a principled cost function for additive models.

tiers.eli5: It is like a team of weak guessers that keep adjusting their votes based on a scoreboard, each new member fixing the mistakes of the group so far.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a boosted classifier with logistic loss, often fitting regression trees as the weak learners. A pitfall is sensitivity to noisy labels and outliers, since the logistic loss keeps responding to hard, possibly mislabeled cases.
tiers.paperLevel: Treating boosting as a generalized additive model and applying the logistic regression cost yields the LogitBoost updates; like other boosting methods it can overfit with too many rounds and needs regularization or early stopping.

explainer.example: On a binary classification dataset, LogitBoost adds trees one at a time, each fitted to the logistic gradient of the current ensemble's errors.
